new_value: Root cause: the six schc_ruleN profile-limit tests constructed packets whose RAW size exceeded SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (22554) while asserting the compressed OUTPUT equals MAX - arithmetically unsatisfiable for every rule (compressed < raw always; empirically rule1 output = raw - 15), so lichen_schc_compress's raw-packet guard (schc.c:538, the fragmenter reassembly bound) rejected before rule dispatch. Fixed the four tail-based tests (rule1/3/4 via TAIL_MAX = MAX - FIXED_RAW; rule2 via PAYLOAD_MAX) to pin the REAL boundary contract: raw == MAX compresses (ret > 0, rule identity pinned via out[0] for rule5/6), raw == MAX+1 rejects SCHC_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL with full-buffer output atomicity. Fixed rule5/6 corrupt-checksum cases to the pre-dispatch drop contract: validate_ipv6_transport_lengths (schc_helpers.c:502-504) rejects checksum mismatch with NO_MATCHING_RULE before rule dispatch per spec/03 'structural or checksum failure MUST be dropped' - the old SCHC_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT expectation pinned a rule-internal path unreachable via the public API (reviewer-verified); replacing it with drop + atomicity is a strengthening. All six suites PASS on gcc-13 (full host sweep 0 build failures, 0 test failures). Follow-ups filed: ly9b (P1: C bounds raw vs Rust bounds encoded - genuine cross-impl divergence in the raw band (22554, 22583], needs a spec decision); review P3s addressed in-round (rule5/6 rule-identity pins, rules 1-4 full-buffer atomicity). Note: spec/03:118 confirms rules 2/3/4 intentionally ignore the ICMPv6 checksum (Rule 255 fallback), so only the UDP rules carry the checksum-strict comments.
